oil.when: 2023 with the Oil Change Reminder in the infotainment Setup menu
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed. Resetting early makes the reminder show the wrong oil life.
With the vehicle parked and switched on, tap Setup on the infotainment screen.
Choose Vehicle, then Cluster, then Oil Change Reminder. This screen shows the remaining oil life.
Select Reset, and choose Yes if the screen asks whether the engine oil has been changed.
Check that the oil life now reads 100%.
oil.note: The reminder warns at 5% and again at 1% oil life. It does not replace the maintenance schedule, so change the oil on schedule even if no warning has shown.

tpms.when: 2023 (sensors in each wheel; no reset button)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the label on the driver's door pillar, checking them before driving or after the car has sat a few hours.
There is no reset button or menu to press: this system reads the new pressures by itself.
Drive the car normally. The tire pressures show in the gauge cluster after a short distance, and the readings are only accurate once the car has been driven.
Check that all four readings in the cluster now match the door label. The low tire pressure light should go out once the system reads the corrected pressures.
If the light comes back on, a tire may be leaking. Recheck the pressures and have the tire inspected.
tpms.note: If the tire pressure light blinks for about a minute and then stays on, the monitoring system itself has a fault. Correct pressures will not clear it, so have a Genesis service location check it. Cold weather can lower pressures enough to turn the light on.
